text:
anya: Heads up — following the GitHub Actions quickstart for the sample-app. Locally curl with my API key returns 200, but the CI job in my forked PR fails with 402 PaymentRequired on the first SDK call. Wondering if this is a billing issue or a secrets problem.

ci-bot: Workflow run #78 for branch anya/onboard-demo failed: Step "Run sample integration" exited with status 1. See https://github.com/redwood/sample-app/actions/runs/12345.

mateo: Common trap: secrets are not available to workflows from forked PRs. If the sample relies on a repo secret (REDWOOD_API_KEY) the container will run without it. What env did the action try to use?

anya: The workflow uses `secrets.REDWOOD_API_KEY` and injects it into the container as REDWOOD_API_KEY. Logs inside the job show `REDWOOD_API_KEY=` (empty). The SDK printed `PaymentRequired workspace_unbilled`. Locally I have REDWOOD_API_KEY set and it works.

mateo: That matches. When the key is empty the request sometimes gets mapped to an anonymous or workspace-limited token and the gateway returns 402 rather than 401 depending on routing. The error message is confusing in CI because it looks like a billing problem.

security: Also check that the secret is the right key type. We have personal keys and workspace keys; CI should use a workspace key scoped to the proper workspace or a service account token. Personal keys sometimes are blocked in org-level CI policies.

anya: Good call. This is a forked PR on a community repo; I don't have access to org secrets so I forked then opened PR. The forked workflow can't read the upstream repo secrets by design.

mateo: Two pragmatic fixes: (1) update the sample CI to run a short smoke mode for forked PRs that uses a mock server or the public REST echo endpoint instead of live calls, (2) surface a clearer CI-friendly error when the SDK sees no key at startup: fail fast with `Missing API key: set REDWOOD_API_KEY (CI workflows: secrets are not available to forked PRs)` instead of retrying and surfacing 402.

anya: I also noticed the sample's workflow masks the variable in logs but doesn't confirm presence; adding an explicit `if: env.REDWOOD_API_KEY == ''` check early would produce a clear failure mode.

devex: Action items: (A) Docs: add a short paragraph in quickstart CI section about forked PRs and secrets, (B) Samples: add smoke/mock mode for untrusted PR runs and a `check-secrets` step that fails with a helpful message, (C) SDK: on client init detect empty key and suggest CI-specific guidance in the error text, (D) Security: recommend using a workspace-scoped service token for CI and document rotation practice.

security: We should also advise maintainers to gate workflows with `pull_request_target` carefully; using it exposes secrets to untrusted code. Recommend `pull_request` + explicit maintainers-run for secrets.

anya: I've opened a draft PR to sample-app: https://github.com/redwood/sample-app/pull/321 — adds a `check-secrets` step that prints a clear message and skips live calls for forked PRs.

mateo: I'll file RED-8111 to update SDK error strings for missing/empty keys with CI hints and to short-circuit retries on auth absence.

docs: I'll add the CI section: how GitHub Actions secrets behave with forks, recommended pattern (mock live calls for forks), and sample `check-secrets` snippet.

anya: After adjusting the workflow to skip live calls for the fork, the PR job passes (it runs the mock path). First successful local call still works when I run the integration job with my personal secret.

devex: Great outcome. This thread will go into the onboarding playbook as "CI/forked-PR secrets -> 402 trap". Thanks for the clear reproduction and PR.
